articles.title: Disaster Recovery for Multi-Region Kafka at Uber
articles.read_scope: Complete article prose from Apache Kafka at Uber through conclusion/acknowledgements, including offset-mapping examples and diagram captions; diagram image pixels not inspected.

practice.trigger: Consumer recovery moves between independently replicated or aggregated logs.
practice.failure: Copying a numeric position can skip required events or repeat effects.
practice.mechanism: Bind progress to source identity; translate retained mappings conservatively and reconcile duplicates.
practice.conditions: Usable mapping history, known replication coverage, correct target identity, exclusive ownership where effects require it.
practice.limits: Asynchronous replication can leave unavailable source tail data. Uber's topology and custom mapping are not universal Kafka behavior.
practice.counterexample: A restart within the same intact log does not need cross-cluster translation.
practice.verification: Permute two-source interleaving; compare effect identities, not equal numeric offsets; reject missing recovery evidence.

articles.title: Delivering billions of messages exactly once
articles.publisher: Segment engineering, now hosted by Twilio
articles.read_scope: Complete article body: problem, topology, RocksDB performance/deletion code, snapshots, output-topic reconciliation, production results, and abandoned Memcached approach. Code inspected, not copied or executed.

practice.trigger: Capacity pressure evicts identity evidence or restore rewinds it independently of publication.
practice.failure: An old operation appears new; a remembered but unpublished event is skipped.
practice.mechanism: Measure usable history and reconcile identity state with authoritative output before resumption.
practice.conditions: Stable IDs, retained publication evidence, and a supported way to resolve concurrent publication.
practice.limits: The article omits a complete arbitrary-interleaving proof. Its observed retention is historical, not a current promise.
practice.counterexample: Lifetime durable uniqueness may make an evictable cache nonauthoritative.
practice.verification: Force early eviction and restore both directions of identity/output mismatch; hold inconclusive outcomes.

articles.title: Incident report on June 22, 2026
articles.date_note: Displayed article date; described incident continued through 2026-06-23.
articles.read_scope: Complete article body: impact, proposed changes, full timeline, causes, recovery sequence, reservation/backlog problems, second-region failure, and closing status.

practice.trigger: Regional failover or cold recovery with admitted work awaiting execution.
practice.failure: Stranded reservations block healthy capacity; restart demand collapses recovering coordination.
practice.mechanism: Separate admission, reservation, execution, and completion; recover ownership and ramp observed useful capacity.
practice.conditions: Inspect actual scheduler states, shared limits, late pickups, retention, and available downstream headroom.
practice.limits: Planned fixes are not shipped evidence. The incident is not proof that maintenance consumes a business-failure attempt.
practice.counterexample: Blindly releasing a possibly running task's slot can permit duplicate concurrent execution.
practice.verification: Strand reservations, race an old pickup with transfer, and check concurrency plus eventual completion.

official_crosschecks.title: MirrorMaker Configs
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Targeted source/checkpoint configuration entries: offset-sync emission/location, group/topic filters, checkpoint emission, automatic translated group-offset synchronization and intervals.
official_crosschecks.finding: Offset syncs support translation; automatic group-offset installation defaults off and requires no active consumers of that group on the target.

official_crosschecks.title: Geo-Replication (Cross-Cluster Data Mirroring)
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Overview/replication flows, configuration and exactly-once section, topic/group filters, and monitoring; not every linked connector source file.
official_crosschecks.finding: Inter-cluster mirroring differs from broker replication. Exactly-once mirroring is separately configured; source read_committed visibility and upgrade conditions matter. It does not cover arbitrary external application effects.

official_crosschecks.title: Handling Duplicate Data
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Complete substantive page, including ingress, warehouse, and data-lake distinctions.
official_crosschecks.finding: Current ingress contract describes approximately 24-hour/99% duplicate suppression based on messageId; destination behavior differs. The historical four-week result must not become a present guarantee.

official_crosschecks.title: Replay
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Complete substantive page: tooling/resilience, eligibility, disabled destinations, filters, integrations/consent, and Engage replay versus resync.
official_crosschecks.finding: Replay may reach disabled destinations, uses destination filters, and has destination-specific deduplication. Historical Engage replay can replace newer state; current-state resync is a distinct operation.

official_crosschecks.title: Runs
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Targeted initial states, attempts/completion, boolean state helpers, cancel/replay operations, and queued TTL sections.
official_crosschecks.finding: DEQUEUED and EXECUTING count toward concurrency; WAITING does not. A queued run can expire under TTL, so an incident's no-loss observation is not an unlimited retention promise.

official_crosschecks.title: Concurrency & Queues
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Concurrency model and shared limits, subtask/wait behavior, checkpoint slot release/reacquisition, pause/resume sections.
official_crosschecks.finding: Broad queued-versus-executing language must be read with the run-state contract. Checkpointed waits release slots; resumed work reacquires them. Pausing a queue leaves executing work running.

gaps.already_covered: Projection rebuild must preserve business effects; stale snapshots and historical schema meaning require validation.

verification_proposals.schedule: Source A1,A2,B1,B2; target B1,B2,A1,A2; completed A1,A2. Copy next-offset 2, then compare a conservative translated restart.
verification_proposals.bad_control: Copied position skips both required B events.
verification_proposals.oracle: All four logical identities complete once under the effect ledger; absent mapping or absent required history blocks acceptance or reports loss.
verification_proposals.limit: Does not establish MirrorMaker configuration, replication durability, or a general mapping algorithm.

verification_proposals.schedule: Restore dedup state behind retained output and then ahead of it; introduce a delayed old publisher and unavailable output evidence.
verification_proposals.bad_control: Treating absent identity as fresh duplicates publication; treating identity alone as completion skips publication.
verification_proposals.oracle: Authoritative publication evidence resolves both mismatches; unarbitrated late publication or missing evidence leaves an explicit hold.
verification_proposals.limit: An in-memory log cannot prove broker transactions or external provider outcomes.

verification_proposals.schedule: Exceed a partition's capacity bound while a repeat remains within the promised retry horizon.
verification_proposals.bad_control: Unexpired TTL is assumed sufficient despite identity eviction.
verification_proposals.oracle: Retained-coverage failure is visible and cannot silently authorize a new business effect.
verification_proposals.limit: Requires actual storage/load testing before making a production retention promise.

verification_proposals.schedule: Reserve two global slots in an unavailable region, transfer eligibility, race a late old pickup and old cleanup with successor admission.
verification_proposals.bad_control: Keeping all reservations prevents progress; blindly clearing them permits excess or duplicate execution.
verification_proposals.oracle: At most two accepted executions, eventual useful completion, and stale pickup/release rejection at the authoritative boundary.
verification_proposals.limit: Does not establish scheduler implementation or cold-recovery throughput.

verification_proposals.schedule: Replay an older event into newer destination state with changed replay filters and disabled destination status.
verification_proposals.bad_control: Historical state overwrites newer state or a disabled flag is mistaken for effect isolation.
verification_proposals.oracle: Version-aware replay or explicit current-state reconciliation reaches intended state; actual replay destination/effect policy is enforced.
verification_proposals.limit: Product-specific transformation, consent, and destination behavior need their own integration checks.

limits: No new runtime experiments, model evaluations, skill edits, or infrastructure changes were performed.
Two historical retrospectives and one incident are evidence for mechanisms, not a prevalence ranking.
Current documentation was checked on the access date; no provider or broker deployment was tested.
Existing transactional outbox, acknowledgement, poison-input, historical-schema, and replay-retention guidance remains the baseline; corroboration is not labeled a new gap.
